newsitem.title: TURKEY: New Turkey sell-off chief pledges new initiatives.
newsitem.headline: New Turkey sell-off chief pledges new initiatives.

text.p: The new acting chairman of Turkey's Privatisation Administration (OIB) said the country's sell-off programme is to be revitalised after faltering during the change of government.
"There has been a delay of one month. We will continue our work at speed to make up for this delay," the OIB's Yalcin Atli told Reuters.
Major sell-offs such as petrochemical company Petkim, refiner Tupras and petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi have been held up by political uncertainty, he said.
"Now with the government's determination on privatisation and political stability the way has been opened for these big projects," he said.
He said work was ongoing on assessing the value of new mobile telephone service licenses. "Concession agreements will be signed by the end of the year."
He added the Privatisation Administration was also aiming to execute the sale of a first tranche in state telecommunications company Turk Telekom by the end of the year.
Atli also mentioned new projects such as separate sales of properties belonging to state enterprises included in the privatisation scheme and the establishment of real estate trusts.
Turkey's Higher Board of Privatisation (OYK) headed by the Prime Minister has the final say in privatisation deals. It had last met on March 20 before the change in government took place in June.

Two troubled tenders are expected to come before the OYK at its next meeting -- the block sale of a 30-40 percent stake in flat steel giant Eregli Demir ve Celik Fabrikalari and the block sale of public Etibank.

The Eregli tender where only two bids were received in January was cancelled by a Turkish court last week. The OIB has not held any negotiations with the bidders. Ankara newsroom +90-312-446 2940 DAR EKS
